title: covariance contravariance invariant types and delegates
concepts: Variance describes safe conversions between constructed generic interfaces or delegates whose type arguments have an inheritance relationship. Covariance preserves the direction for produced values; contravariance reverses it for consumed values; invariance permits neither conversion.

The `out` and `in` annotations on interface and delegate type parameters are contracts about how those parameters are used. A producer can be covariant; a consumer can be contravariant; mutable read/write abstractions usually must be invariant to remain safe.

Variance conversions are implicit reference conversions with specific boundaries. They do not make arbitrary generic classes variant, do not apply to value-type arguments, do not change a collection's mutability, and do not make delegate combination accept different delegate types.

Array covariance and generic variance are different mechanisms. Array covariance is available for reference-type arrays but permits an invalid store to fail at runtime; generic interface variance preserves type safety through the interface contract.

Variance and method-group binding are related but separate: a method returning a more derived type or accepting a less derived parameter can bind to a delegate signature. C# 9 also added covariant return types for overrides; that feature is not generic variance.

scopeExclusions: Delegate declarations, events, lambdas, closures, and expression trees are covered in t01-011; this topic covers only variance relevant to their types.
Generic type constraints and inference are covered in t01-009.
Inheritance, virtual dispatch, and interface implementation are covered in t01-007.
Array APIs and generic collection operations are covered in t01-014.
accuracyFacts: Do not reduce interface variance safety to simple return-versus-parameter positions: nested generic/delegate variance composes, and static non-virtual, non-abstract interface members are exempt from variance-safety restrictions.
Do not claim an entire covariant interface or its implementation is immutable; variance safety constrains access through the variant contract.
